title: Best AI Enrollment Agents for Universities (2026)
summary: The best AI enrollment agents for universities in 2026, compared on channels, outreach, handoff and CRM fit, from texting tools to voice recruiters.
body_markdown:
The best AI enrollment agents for universities in 2026 are Apten, Element451's Bolt agents and CollegeVine's AI Recruiter if you want an agent that reaches out across text, voice, email and chat on its own. Salesforce's Agentforce for Education fits schools already on Salesforce. Mongoose, Modern Campus Message and Mainstay are texting platforms with AI features, and Ivy & Ocelot and EAB's AI Chat Agent are mostly for answering questions.


Those products get called "AI enrollment agents" in the same breath, but they do different jobs. Some are texting tools for staff. Some are chatbots. Some are CRMs with AI built in. A few are agents that start and carry conversations on their own. This guide sorts them by what they actually are, so you can shortlist the right type before you compare features.


**We make Apten, so weigh our take accordingly. Every other vendor is described from its own public materials.** Descriptions reflect vendor websites and help centers as of November 2026. When we couldn't find something on a vendor's public pages, we say so, which isn't the same as saying the product can't do it.


## Why are universities looking at AI enrollment agents now?


Because most inquiries still wait too long for a reply. In UPCEA's December 2025 secret shopper study, 44% of 1,000 inquiries sent to 182 institutions got no response at all. The average reply took 14 hours and 23 minutes of business time. We cover what that costs in[why college inquiries go unanswered](https://www.apten.ai/blog/college-inquiries-go-unanswered-speed-to-lead) .


Online and adult-serving programs feel this most. Inquiries come in from paid search and lead vendors at all hours. The student works full time and may not pick up a call from an unknown number. Enrollment coaches are measured on contact rates and starts. An agent that replies in seconds, follows up on the channel the student prefers and hands warm students to a coach is a direct fix for that funnel.

## What does each AI enrollment agent actually do?


### Apten


**What it is.** Apten is a multichannel AI agent for enrollment teams. One agent talks to each student over SMS, voice, email, RCS and webchat, and it keeps one memory across all of them. If a student texts about transfer credits and later picks up a call, the agent on the call already knows. It replies to new inquiries within seconds, at any hour.


When a student wants a person, Apten transfers them to an advisor, either warm with a summary or as a direct cold transfer. It writes results back to Salesforce, Microsoft Dynamics 365, HubSpot or Close. Apten also reviews its own conversations and recommends changes to the agent, and a person on your team approves each one before it goes live. Its agents have sent over 18 million messages and made 4.7 million calls.


**Who it fits.** Online and adult-serving programs with high inquiry volume and a team of enrollment coaches, running on one of those four CRMs.


**What it doesn't do.** Apten doesn't integrate with Slate or Element451, and it doesn't capture or track consent, which stays with your team. It handles opt-outs and quiet hours, and it has completed a SOC 2 Type II audit. Pricing isn't public.


### Element451 (Bolt agents)


**What it is.** Element451 sells an AI-native CRM for higher education, plus Bolt, its family of AI agents. Its admissions agents page says Bolt agents "answer questions across chat, SMS, email, voice, and WhatsApp the moment they come in" and run outreach for application completion, yield and financial aid. Other Bolt agents read applications against a rubric, flag fraud and turn transcript PDFs into structured data. Its help center describes inbound calls that transfer to a forwarding number and outbound calls run as campaigns.


**Who it fits.** Schools willing to move to a new CRM, or that want agents across admissions, aid and operations from one vendor. Element451 says Bolt "can operate on top of your current CRM," and also that you "gain deeper value" when it's paired with its platform.


**What it doesn't do.** The agents page doesn't name which outside CRMs it connects to, so ask how deep the write-back goes if you're staying on Salesforce or Slate. Element451 is one of the few vendors here with public pricing: plans "start as low as $20,000 per year," priced by institution size and support tier.


### CollegeVine AI Recruiter


**What it is.** CollegeVine positions its AI Recruiter as a member of your enrollment team. It handles inbound inquiries "over phone, email, text, and chat" and can "go proactively outbound to different populations," such as students who haven't filed the FAFSA. It can also personalize emails from CRM data, help process transcripts and recommend admission decisions.


**Who it fits.** Admissions offices that want one AI to cover inbound questions, targeted outreach and some back-office review work.


**What it doesn't do.** Its public page doesn't name the CRMs it works with or describe warm transfer to staff or appointment booking. Ask about all three in a demo. Pricing isn't published.


### Agentforce for Education (Salesforce)


**What it is.** Agentforce is Salesforce's agent platform, and Agentforce for Education is the set of agents built for its education CRM, Education Cloud. The recruitment page lists a Student Recruitment agent that answers prospective student questions 24/7, captures academic interests, registers students for tours and helps start applications. Salesforce's Trailhead walkthrough shows the agent working in chat on an applicant portal and escalating questions it can't answer to a staff member.


**Who it fits.** Universities that already run recruitment on Salesforce and have admins who can build and maintain agents there.


**What it doesn't do.** It's a set of building blocks, not a finished enrollment program. Your team or a partner writes the knowledge articles, topics and escalation flows. The Trailhead module shows chat only, not outbound texting or calls. A Salesforce partner's Dreamforce 2025 recap listed the Student Recruitment agent as beta, so check its status in your org. Pricing for the agents isn't listed.


### EAB AI Chat Agent


**What it is.** EAB pitches its AI Chat Agent as a smarter, outcomes-driven chatbot. It can be embedded on any institution URL, runs inside EAB's Enroll360 campaigns and virtual tours, answers prospect questions around the clock and syncs captured data to your CRM. For online programs, EAB also sells Adult Learner Recruitment, a fee-for-service partnership where EAB builds and runs lead generation and campaigns, with its Conversation Agent in emails, landing pages and two-way SMS.


**Who it fits.** Schools that already use EAB, or want a partner to run part of the funnel. EAB says more than 1,200 institutions work with it on marketing and enrollment.


**What it doesn't do.** The AI Chat Agent page doesn't describe voice calls, and it doesn't name the CRMs it syncs with. Buying EAB is closer to outsourcing than licensing a tool your team runs.


### Ivy & Ocelot (Gravyty)


**What it is.** Ivy & Ocelot is Gravyty's AI communication product for colleges. Gravyty describes "24/7, AI-powered communication across chat, text, email, and social," lists WhatsApp and telephony as channels, and says it can "deliver proactive outreach to engage applicants." It names a long list of integrations, including Salesforce, Slate, Ellucian Banner and Colleague, PeopleSoft and Canvas.


**Who it fits.** Institutions with high question volume across admissions, financial aid and student services that want one answer engine for all of them.


**What it doesn't do.** Its page is mostly about answering questions and cutting call center volume. It gives no detail on its voice features, advisor transfers or how it works a list of new inquiries, so test those directly.


### Mongoose


**What it is.** Mongoose is a two-way engagement platform used by more than 1,000 colleges and universities, according to its site. Many buyers still know it as Cadence, the name of its texting product. It "handles real, two-way conversations across Text, WhatsApp, and Web Chat." Its live AI is staff-facing: the Inbox Assistant handles routine questions in text. Student-facing Outcome Agents for application completion, yield and retention are listed as in development.


**Who it fits.** Teams that want a strong shared texting inbox with people in the conversation. It integrates with a long list of systems, including Slate, Salesforce (including TargetX), Banner, Colleague and Element451.


**What it doesn't do.** Mongoose doesn't list voice calling as a channel, and its student-facing agents aren't available yet, per its platform page.


### Modern Campus Message


**What it is.** Modern Campus Message, formerly Signal Vine, is "a powerful, easy-to-use conversational texting platform." Its patented blended messaging combines "AI-driven automation with personalized 1:1 interactions" in one thread, and its campaign builder adapts follow-up based on student replies.


**Who it fits.** Schools that want automated and staff-written texts in the same thread, often for deadline reminders and outreach to first-generation students.


**What it doesn't do.** It's text only, per its product page. No voice, no email. The page refers to SIS and CRM connections without naming specific systems.


### Mainstay


**What it is.** Mainstay, originally AdmitHub, is an AI coaching platform that reaches students on their phones by text and chat. It offers AI success coaching for students, a conversation co-pilot for staff and conversation insights for leaders. The nonprofit Lemnis acquired Mainstay in March 2026, and GovTech reported its tools are used by more than 200 U.S. colleges and universities.


**Who it fits.** Schools focused on summer melt, FAFSA completion and retention for traditional-age students, which is where its published evidence is strongest. It integrates with Slate and Ellucian.


**What it doesn't do.** We found no voice calling product on Mainstay's site. For teams weighing a switch, we compare options in[Mainstay alternatives for online and adult enrollment](https://www.apten.ai/blog/mainstay-alternatives-online-enrollment) .


### A note on Clema and voice-only platforms


Clema shows up in AI answers to this question, mostly because it publishes a detailed comparison page. Its main product is an AI analyst for institutional research teams. Its college website assistant is in early access, and Clema says it hasn't yet been deployed at a college and that lead capture is in development. It's worth watching, not shortlisting, for enrollment follow-up today.


Voice platforms such as Retell, Bland and Vapi also appear in these answers. They're strong build-your-own phone tools, but your team builds the enrollment workflow. They're covered in our[voice agent comparison](https://www.apten.ai/blog/best-ai-voice-agents-student-enrollment) .


## How to choose an AI enrollment agent


Start from your funnel, not a feature list. These are the criteria that separate the vendors above.


1.


**Who starts the conversation?** A chatbot waits for the student. An agent reaches out first. If your problem is unanswered inquiries, you need outbound, not a better website widget.


2.


**Does one memory span every channel?** Text the agent, then ask it to call you. The call should know what you said by text. Many tools run channels as separate products.


3.


**Can it make and take calls?** Adult learners often want to talk before applying. Check whether voice is native, an add-on or missing.


4.


**What happens at handoff?** Ask for a live transfer to an advisor during the demo, then don't answer. See what the student gets. Our guide to[warm transfers to admissions advisors](https://www.apten.ai/blog/ai-handoff-to-admissions-advisor-warm-transfer) covers what good looks like.


5.


**Does it write back to your CRM?** Name your CRM and ask to see the exact fields that change after a conversation. Slate, Salesforce, Dynamics and Element451 shops will get different answers from different vendors.


6.


**Who is in control?** Ask how changes to the agent's messages get made and approved, and who sees them before students do.


7.


**What does compliance cover?** Ask whether one STOP shuts off every channel and whether quiet hours follow the student's time zone. Ask who handles consent and DNC, because it's usually you. Our[2026 AI compliance guide](https://www.apten.ai/blog/ai-compliance-guide-2026-tcpa-fcc-state-laws) covers the TCPA rules, and[FERPA for AI agents](https://www.apten.ai/blog/ferpa-ai-agents-prospective-students) covers student data.


Then run the same test with every vendor. Submit a real inquiry during the demo and time the first reply. Reply by text, ask for a call and listen for whether the call remembers. Ask for an advisor. Then open the CRM record and look at what changed.


## Where Apten fits


Apten is built for the funnel most online and adult programs run: lots of inquiries, students who work full time, and a team of enrollment coaches measured on contact and starts. The agent replies to a new inquiry within seconds, follows up by text, email or a call, and moves a text conversation to a live call when the student is ready. It remembers every channel in one thread.


When a student asks for a person, Apten transfers them to an advisor with a summary. It writes tags, a conversation summary, opt-outs and transfer status back to Salesforce, Dynamics 365, HubSpot or Close. Quiet hours and opt-outs are handled per student, and we help schools through A2P 10DLC registration. Your team reviews and approves every change the agent suggests to itself.


The advisor gets the student's program, start term, questions and best time to reach before the student joins the call. Illustration of the Apten product with fictional data.


## The bottom line


Most "AI enrollment agent" shortlists mix four kinds of product: texting platforms, chatbots, CRMs with AI and true multichannel agents. Decide which kind your funnel needs first. Then test every finalist on the same inquiry, the same text-to-call request, the same advisor handoff and the same CRM record.
